phrases: how to keep my account safe
how do i secure my account
how can i protect my account
how do i know it's a scam
bank will never ask for otp
intents.response:
To keep your online banking safe, follow these security tips (especially for Internet banking / mobile app):

1) Protect your login (most important)
- Never share your password, passcode, or any one-time codes (OTP / verification codes).
- Never share your full card details, PIN, CVV, or credentials.
- Only sign in using the official bank app or by typing the official website address yourself (do not open banking from links in SMS/email).
- If you suspect someone has your credentials, change your password immediately and sign out of other devices.

2) OTP / approvals safety (OTP scams)
- Banks will never ask you to share OTP/verification codes with anyone (including “bank staff”, “fraud team”, or “IT support”).
- If someone asks for your OTP, treat it as a scam and stop immediately.
- If you already shared an OTP (or you received an OTP you didn’t request):
  a) Stop talking to the caller/scammer.
  b) Change your password right away.
  c) Check your recent transactions/beneficiaries in the app.
  d) Freeze your card / block suspicious activity if available.
  e) Contact support so they can secure your account and review activity.

3) Beware of phishing (SMS/email/calls) and fake bank pages
- Don’t click links or open attachments from unexpected messages.
- Check the sender and the exact message wording; scammers often mimic urgency and official language.
- If a message claims something like “your account will be locked” or “verify now”, don’t panic.
- Open the bank app directly instead of using a link.
- If you clicked a link:
  a) Do not enter OTP/password.
  b) Close the page/app and go to the official app/website manually.
  c) If you entered credentials, change your password.
  d) If your phone feels compromised (popups, unknown apps), secure your device and contact support.

4) Safe transfers and payment scams
Scammers often try to trick you into approving transfers you didn’t intend.
- Always verify the beneficiary/recipient details inside the app before confirming.
- If anyone pressures you to act fast ("act now", "urgent transfer", "payment pending"), pause and verify in the app.
- If you’re asked to change beneficiary details or share screen/remote access: stop.
- If you suspect a transfer scam:
  a) Do not confirm any new transfer.
  b) Check the transaction list in your app for recent outflows.
  c) If you see an unauthorized transaction, freeze/block cards (if relevant) and raise a dispute.
  d) Contact support immediately for investigation.

5) Secure your device (reduce takeover risk)
- Keep your phone updated (OS updates) and keep the bank app updated.
- Install apps only from trusted stores.
- Avoid banking on public/shared Wi‑Fi when possible; if you must, use a trusted connection.
- Watch for signs of compromise: frequent popups, unknown admin access, unexpected apps, browser redirects.
- If compromised: remove unknown apps, run security checks, and change your password.

6) SIM swap / number takeover (when scammers can intercept OTP)
- Never share your SIM/phone verification PIN or any OTP.
- If you notice sudden loss of network or your number is “not registered”, treat it as possible SIM swap.
- Contact your telecom provider quickly, and then contact bank support so they can secure your account.

7) What to do right now (quick checklist)
Reply with the closest option:
- "OTP requested" (someone asked for OTP/verification code)
- "Clicked a link" (phishing site / suspicious URL)
- "Transfer scam" (someone pushed me to transfer or change beneficiary)
- "Device looks compromised" (popups/unknown apps)
- "I think my account was accessed" (unknown login or changes)

Then I’ll guide you step-by-step on the exact actions to take in the app and what to report.

If you want, tell me what happened in one sentence (example: "I got an sms asking for otp" or "someone asked me to transfer money"), and I’ll tailor the steps.
intents.short_response: If someone is asking you for OTP/verification codes, it’s a scam. Stop talking to them and do this now: (1) never share the OTP, (2) change your password, (3) check recent transactions/beneficiaries in the app, and (4) contact support so they can secure your account.
